chunks: One of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Shaykh's companions, from Ali ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

Dreams did not exist in the past at the beginning of creation, but rather they occurred later. I said, 'And what is the reason for that?' He said, 'Allah, Exalted is His mention, sent a Messenger to the people of his time and called them to the worship of Allah and His obedience. They said, 'If we do that, what is in it for us? By Allah, you are not wealthier than us, nor is your clan stronger than ours.' He said, 'If you obey me, Allah will make you enter Paradise, and if you disobey me, Allah will make you enter the Fire.' They said, 'And what is Paradise and the Fire?' So he described that for them. They said, 'When do we go to that?' He said, 'When you die.' They said, 'We have seen our dead become bones and dust.' So they increased in their denial and contempt of it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, caused dreams to occur among them. So they came to him and informed him of what they saw and what they had denied from that. He said, 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intended to establish the argument against you by this. This is how your spirits will be when you die, and even if your bodies decay, the spirits will go to punishment until the bodies are resurrected.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Allah introduce dreams to prove resurrection?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that dreams were a later divine innovation, serving as a tangible proof (hujjah) for resurrection to a people who doubted it because they saw their bodies turn to dust. By experiencing the soul's separation during sleep, they could intuitively grasp that the spirit persists independently of the decaying body, thereby validating the promise of bodily resurrection. This narrative highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on dreams as a metaphysical bridge between the physical and spiritual realms, reinforcing the concept of barzakh.
